title: DC-area forecast: Showers wind down this evening; drier and milder Monday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Showers diminish early to mid-evening with an isolated shower possible overnight. Winds gradually ease with temperatures around 60 through the night.

What's next? Drier weather Monday with less winds and somewhat warmer highs near 70. Building sunshine and warmth midweek.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Showers, most numerous through early evening, become more isolated overnight. Winds gradually ease from gusty afternoon levels. Any patchy fog should thin a bit later in the evening and overnight, but remaining cloudy with temperatures fairly steady near 60. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow (Monday): Mostly cloudy skies linger with a few peeks of sun possible. Any lingering shower chance is minimal — perhaps a stray shower or sprinkle. Afternoon highs in the upper 60s to low 70s remain a bit cooler than average. Winds from the northwest gust much less, perhaps near 20 mph a couple times. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly cloudy and calming breezes. The tiniest chance of a stray pop-up shower. Lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Partly sunny and pleasantly warmer Tuesday with highs in the more seasonable mid-70s. Partly cloudy Tuesday night with lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

Hopefully your shorts aren’t too far out of reach. High pressure positioned off the coast delivers a warming breeze from the south Wednesday and Thursday. Highs head for the upper 70s to low 80s Wednesday, and low to mid-80s Thursday, under partly to mostly sunny skies. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: A September nor'easter continues to sweep in cloudy skies, gusty winds, and cool vibes – oh, and some showers too. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 27
